Cholesteatoma.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Cholesteatoma.question: The _____ was Tumor of the middle ear.
Cholesteatoma.fact: Cholesteatoma is a destructive and expanding growth consisting of keratinizing, squamous epithelium in the middle ear and/or mastoid process. Conductive hearing loss.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Conductive hearing loss.question: This can be an isolated phenomenon or may occur as part of a syndrome where development of the 1st and 2nd branchial arches is seen, such as in Goldenhar syndrome, Treacher Collins syndrome, _____, etc
Conductive hearing loss.fact: This can be an isolated phenomenon or may occur as part of a syndrome where development of the 1st and 2nd branchial arches is seen, such as in Goldenhar syndrome, Treacher Collins syndrome, branchio-oto-renal syndrome, etc.

Conductive hearing loss.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Conductive hearing loss.question: It is managed by any of various methods of ear clearing manoeuvres to equalize the pressures, like swallowing, yawning, or the _____ manoeuvre
Conductive hearing loss.fact: It is managed by any of various methods of ear clearing manoeuvres to equalize the pressures, like swallowing, yawning, or the Valsalva manoeuvre.

Conductive hearing loss.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Conductive hearing loss.question: With a one-sided conductive component, the combined use of both the _____ and Rinne tests is useful
Conductive hearing loss.fact: With a one-sided conductive component, the combined use of both the Weber and Rinne tests is useful. If the Weber test is used, in which a vibrating tuning fork is touched to the midline of the forehead, the person will hear the sound more loudly in the affected ear because background noise does not mask the hearing on this side.

Appendix of testis.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Appendix of testis.question: The _____ was Part of the testis.
Appendix of testis.fact: Torsion of the appendix of testis occurs at ages 0–15 years, with a mean at 10 years, which is similar to that of testicular torsion.

Appendix of testis.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Appendix of testis.question: The appendix testis (or hydatid of _____) is a vestigial remnant of the Müllerian duct, present on the upper pole of the testis and attached to the tunica vaginalis
Appendix of testis.fact: The appendix testis (or hydatid of Morgagni) is a vestigial remnant of the Müllerian duct, present on the upper pole of the testis and attached to the tunica vaginalis.

Appendix of testis.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Appendix of testis.question: It is present about _____ of the time
Appendix of testis.fact: It is present about 90% of the time.

Appendix of the epididymis.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Appendix of the epididymis.question: This structure is derived from the _____ duct (mesonephric duct) as opposed to the appendix testis which is derived from the Müllerian duct (paramesonephric duct) remnant
Appendix of the epididymis.fact: This structure is derived from the Wolffian duct (mesonephric duct) as opposed to the appendix testis which is derived from the Müllerian duct (paramesonephric duct) remnant.

Artery of bulb of penis.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Artery of bulb of penis.question: The _____ was Blood vessel.
Artery of bulb of penis.fact: The artery of bulb of penis (artery of the urethral bulb or bulbourethral artery) is a short artery of large caliber which arises from the internal pudendal artery between the two layers of fascia (the superior and inferior) of the urogenital diaphragm.

Blood–testis barrier.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Blood–testis barrier.question: The _____ was Physical barrier between the blood vessels and the seminiferous tubules of animal testes.
Blood–testis barrier.fact: The blood–testis barrier is a physical barrier between the blood vessels and the seminiferous tubules of the animal testes.

Blood–testis barrier.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Blood–testis barrier.question: A more correct term is the _____ cell barrier (SCB)
Blood–testis barrier.fact: The name "blood-testis barrier" is misleading as it is not a blood-organ barrier in a strict sense, but is formed between Sertoli cells of the seminiferous tubule and isolates the further developed stages of germ cells from the blood. A more correct term is the Sertoli cell barrier (SCB).

Blood–testis barrier.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Blood–testis barrier.question: For the visualization of the actin fibers within the seminiferous tubules see _____ et al.'s immunofluorescence studies
Blood–testis barrier.fact: For the visualization of the actin fibers within the seminiferous tubules see Sharma et al.'s immunofluorescence studies.

Blood–testis barrier.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Blood–testis barrier.question: Some proteins pass from _____ cells to Leydig cells to function in a paracrine fashion
Blood–testis barrier.fact: Some proteins pass from Sertoli cells to Leydig cells to function in a paracrine fashion.

Body of penis.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Body of penis.question: The _____ was Part of the penis located outside of the pelvic cavity.
Body of penis.fact: The body or shaft of the penis is the free portion of the human penis that is located outside of the pelvic cavity. It is the continuation of the internal root, which is embedded in the pelvis and extends to the glans.

Body of penis.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Body of penis.question: The body is ensheathed by fascia, which includes tunica albuginea, _____'s fascia, dermis, and skin
Body of penis.fact: The body is ensheathed by fascia, which includes tunica albuginea, Buck's fascia, dermis, and skin.

Buck's fascia.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Buck's fascia.question: The _____ was Fascia in the penis.
Buck's fascia.fact: Buck's fascia (deep fascia of the penis, Gallaudet's fascia or fascia of the penis) is a layer of deep fascia covering the three erectile bodies of the penis.

Bulb of penis.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Bulb of penis.question: The _____ was Flare of the urethra tissue at the base of the human biological male sex organ.
Bulb of penis.fact: The bulb of penis is the proximal/posterior bulged end of the (unpaired median) corpus spongiosum penis. Proximally/posteriorly, the bulb of penis extends towards the perineal body.

Corpus cavernosum penis.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Corpus cavernosum penis.question: The _____ was Sponge-like region of erectile tissue.
Corpus cavernosum penis.fact: A corpus cavernosum penis (singular) (from Latin, characterised by cavities, or hollows, of the penis, pl.: corpora cavernosa penium) is one of a pair of sponge-like regions of erectile tissue, which contain most of the blood in the penis during an erection in several species of mammals.

Corpus cavernosum penis.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Corpus cavernosum penis.question: A little blood enters the corpus spongiosum; the remainder engorges the corpora cavernosa, which expand to hold _____ of the blood involved in an erection, increasing both in length and in diameter
Corpus cavernosum penis.fact: A little blood enters the corpus spongiosum; the remainder engorges the corpora cavernosa, which expand to hold 90% of the blood involved in an erection, increasing both in length and in diameter.

Corona of glans penis.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Corona of glans penis.question: The _____ was Flare above the sulcus of the human penis.
Corona of glans penis.fact: The corona of glans penis (or, directly from the Latin, the corona glandis penis) or penis crown refers to the rounded projecting border or flare that forms at the base of the glans in human males.

Cremaster muscle.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Cremaster muscle.question: The _____ was Muscle covering the testicles and spermatic cords.
Cremaster muscle.fact: The cremaster muscle is a paired structure made of thin layers of striated and smooth muscle that covers the testicles and the spermatic cords in human males.

Cremaster muscle.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Cremaster muscle.question: The ideal temperature for human sperm development is around 34.5-35 degrees _____, which is about 2-2.5 degrees Celsius below body temperature
Cremaster muscle.fact: The ideal temperature for human sperm development is around 34.5-35 degrees Celsius, which is about 2-2.5 degrees Celsius below body temperature.

Cremaster muscle.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Cremaster muscle.question: The cremaster can also be contracted voluntarily, by performing _____ (which somehow contracts the cremaster), or by flexing and tightening the abdominal muscles
Cremaster muscle.fact: The cremaster can also be contracted voluntarily, by performing Kegels (which somehow contracts the cremaster), or by flexing and tightening the abdominal muscles.

Cremaster muscle.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Cremaster muscle.question: Treatment for these spasms ranges from minor surgery to injection with _____ A toxin to the regular application of heat to relax the muscle
Cremaster muscle.fact: Treatment for these spasms ranges from minor surgery to injection with Botulinum A toxin to the regular application of heat to relax the muscle.

Crus of penis.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Crus of penis.question: The _____ was Internal base of the human biological male sex organ.
Crus of penis.fact: The two crura of penis (one crus on each side) constitute the root of penis along with the bulb of penis. The two crura flank the bulb – one to each side of the bulb.

Dorsal artery of the penis.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Dorsal artery of the penis.question: The _____ was Artery of the penis.
Dorsal artery of the penis.fact: The dorsal artery of the penis is a bilaterally paired terminal branch of the internal pudendal artery which passes upon the dorsum of the penis to the base of the glans penis, where it unites with its contralateral partner and supply the glans and foreskin. The dorsal artery of the penis provides blood supply to the skin and fascia of the penis (including the foreskin), and the erectile tissues of the penis (especially the glans penis).

Dorsal nerve of the penis.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Dorsal nerve of the penis.question: The _____ was Deepest division of the pudendal nerve.
Dorsal nerve of the penis.fact: The dorsal nerve of the penis is the deepest of three divisions of the pudendal nerve; it accompanies the internal pudendal artery along the ramus of the ischium; it then runs forward along the margin of the inferior ramus of the pubis, between the superior and inferior layers of the fascia of the urogenital diaphragm.

Epididymis.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Epididymis.question: The _____ was Tube that connects a testicle to a vas deferens.
Epididymis.fact: The epididymis (; pl.: epididymides or ) is an elongated tubular genital organ attached to the posterior side of each one of the two male reproductive glands, the testicles. The epididymis connects the testicle to the vas deferens in the male reproductive system.

Epididymis.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Epididymis.question: The major cell types in the epithelium are: _____ cells: columnar cells that, with the basal cells, form the majority of the epithelium
Epididymis.fact: The major cell types in the epithelium are: Principal cells: columnar cells that, with the basal cells, form the majority of the epithelium.

Epididymis.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Epididymis.question: Apical cells: predominantly found in the head region Clear cells: predominant in the tail region _____ lymphocytes: distributed throughout the tissue
Epididymis.fact: Apical cells: predominantly found in the head region Clear cells: predominant in the tail region Intraepithelial lymphocytes: distributed throughout the tissue.

Epididymis.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Epididymis.question: This has also been proven in a similar case in _____ in the early 1990s

Epididymis.fact: It is a single, narrow, tightly coiled tube which, in adult humans, is about 6 to 7 centimetres (2.4 to 2.8 in) in length; uncoiled, the tube would be approximately 6 m (20 feet) long.

Epididymis.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Epididymis.question: The core function of the stereocilia is to resorb _____ of this fluid as the spermatozoa start to become motile
Epididymis.fact: The core function of the stereocilia is to resorb 90% of this fluid as the spermatozoa start to become motile.

External spermatic fascia.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
External spermatic fascia.question: The _____ was Thin membrane covering the spermatic cord and testis.
External spermatic fascia.fact: The external spermatic fascia (intercrural or intercolumnar fascia) is a thin membrane, prolonged downward around the surface of the spermatic cord and testis.

External spermatic fascia.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
External spermatic fascia.question: It is occasionally referred to as '_____ de Webster' after an anatomist who once described it
External spermatic fascia.fact: It is occasionally called 'Le Fascia de Webster' after an anatomist who once described it.

External sphincter muscle of male urethr.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
External sphincter muscle of male urethr.subSubject: External sphincter muscle of male urethra
External sphincter muscle of male urethr.question: The _____ was Muscle of the human male urethra.
External sphincter muscle of male urethr.answer: External sphincter muscle of male urethra
External sphincter muscle of male urethr.fact: The external sphincter muscle of the male urethra, also sphincter urethrae membranaceae, sphincter urethrae externus, surrounds the whole length of the membranous urethra, and is enclosed in the fascia of the urogenital diaphragm. Its external fibers arise from the junction of the inferior pubic ramus and ischium to the extent of 1.25 to 2 cm., and from the neighboring fascia.

External sphincter muscle of male urethr.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
External sphincter muscle of male urethr.subSubject: External sphincter muscle of male urethra
External sphincter muscle of male urethr.question: This is facilitated by inhibition of the somatic neurons in _____'s nucleus via signals arising in the pontine micturition center and traveling through the descending reticulospinal tracts
External sphincter muscle of male urethr.fact: The external sphincter muscle prevents urine leakage as the muscle is tonically contracted via somatic fibers that originate in Onuf's nucleus and pass through sacral spinal nerves S2-S4 then the pudendal nerve to synapse on the muscle. This is facilitated by inhibition of the somatic neurons in Onuf's nucleus via signals arising in the pontine micturition center and traveling through the descending reticulospinal tracts.

Ciaccio's glands.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Ciaccio's glands.question: The _____ was Tear glands of the eye.
Ciaccio's glands.fact: Ciaccio's glands or Wolfring's glands are small tubular accessory lacrimal glands (glandulae lacrimales accessoriae) found in the lacrimal caruncle of the eyelid.

Ciaccio's glands.question: They are named after Italian anatomist Giuseppe Vincenzo Ciaccio (_____–1901), who described these glands in 1874

Ciaccio's glands.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy

Dacryocystitis.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Dacryocystitis.question: The _____ was Infection of the lacrimal sac of the eye.
Dacryocystitis.fact: Dacryocystitis is an infection of the lacrimal sac, secondary to obstruction of the nasolacrimal duct at the junction of the lacrimal sac.

Dacryocystitis.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Dacryocystitis.question: The term derives from _____ dákryon 'tear', cysta 'sac' and -itis 'inflammation'
Dacryocystitis.fact: The term derives from Greek dákryon 'tear', cysta 'sac' and -itis 'inflammation'.

Dacryocystitis.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Dacryocystitis.question: It is most commonly caused by _____ aureus and Streptococcus pneumoniae
Dacryocystitis.fact: It is most commonly caused by Staphylococcus aureus and Streptococcus pneumoniae.

Gastrulation.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Gastrulation.question: The _____ was Embryologic stage in which germ layers form.
Gastrulation.fact: Gastrulation is the stage in the early embryonic development of most animals, during which the blastula (a single-layered hollow sphere of cells), or in mammals, the blastocyst, is reorganized into a two-layered or three-layered embryo called the gastrula,with an infold named the blastopore. Before gastrulation, the embryo is a continuous epithelial sheet of cells; by the end of gastrulation, the embryo has begun differentiation to establish distinct cell lineages, set up the basic axes of th...

Gastrulation.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Gastrulation.question: In diploblastic organisms, such as _____ and Ctenophora, the gastrula has only ectoderm and endoderm
Gastrulation.fact: In diploblastic organisms, such as Cnidaria and Ctenophora, the gastrula has only ectoderm and endoderm.

Gastrulation.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Gastrulation.question: Gastrula (literally, "little belly") is a neo-Latin diminutive based on the _____ γαστήρ gastḗr ("a belly")
Gastrulation.fact: Gastrula (literally, "little belly") is a neo-Latin diminutive based on the Ancient Greek γαστήρ gastḗr ("a belly").

Gastrulation.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Gastrulation.question: The organizer, which sits in the center of this process, is a trait conserved among _____, Ctenophora, and Bilateria – all major groups of animals except sponges
Gastrulation.fact: The organizer, which sits in the center of this process, is a trait conserved among Cnidaria, Ctenophora, and Bilateria – all major groups of animals except sponges.

Gastrulation.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Gastrulation.question: Protostome derives from the Greek word protostoma meaning "first mouth" (πρῶτος + στόμα) whereas _____'s etymology is "second mouth" from the words second and mouth (δεύτερος + στόμα)
Gastrulation.fact: Protostome derives from the Greek word protostoma meaning "first mouth" (πρῶτος + στόμα) whereas Deuterostome's etymology is "second mouth" from the words second and mouth (δεύτερος + στόμα). The major distinctions between deuterostomes and protostomes are found in embryonic development: Mouth/anus In protostome development, the first opening in development, the blastopore, becomes the animal's mouth – at least this was the original definition.

Gastrulation.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Gastrulation.question: Canonical Wnt and _____-Notch signaling progressively segregate progressive endoderm and mesoderm
Gastrulation.fact: Canonical Wnt and Delta-Notch signaling progressively segregate progressive endoderm and mesoderm.

Gastrulation.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Gastrulation.question: Other signals such as Wnt and BMP also play a role in respiratory fate of the _____ by activating cell lineage tracers
Gastrulation.fact: Other signals such as Wnt and BMP also play a role in respiratory fate of the Xenopus by activating cell lineage tracers.

Gastrulation.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Gastrulation.question: Formation of the primitive streak is reliant upon nodal signaling in the _____'s sickle within the cells contributing to the primitive streak and BMP4 signaling from the extraembryonic tissue
Gastrulation.fact: Formation of the primitive streak is reliant upon nodal signaling in the Koller's sickle within the cells contributing to the primitive streak and BMP4 signaling from the extraembryonic tissue.

Gastrulation.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Gastrulation.question: Furthermore, Cer1 and _____1 restrict the primitive streak to the appropriate location by antagonizing nodal signaling
Gastrulation.fact: Furthermore, Cer1 and Lefty1 restrict the primitive streak to the appropriate location by antagonizing nodal signaling.

Gastrulation.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Gastrulation.question: FGFR1 is needed for the up regulation of _____1, which down regulates E-cadherin, causing a loss of cell adhesion
Gastrulation.fact: FGFR1 is needed for the up regulation of SNAI1, which down regulates E-cadherin, causing a loss of cell adhesion.

Gastrulation.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Gastrulation.question: These ligands will signal transmembrane serine/threonine kinase receptors, and this will then phosphorylate _____2 and Smad3
Gastrulation.fact: These ligands will signal transmembrane serine/threonine kinase receptors, and this will then phosphorylate Smad2 and Smad3. This protein will then attach itself to Smad4 and relocate to the nucleus where the mesendoderm genes will begin to be transcribed.

Gastrulation.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Gastrulation.question: This protein will then attach itself to _____4 and relocate to the nucleus where the mesendoderm genes will begin to be transcribed
Gastrulation.fact: These ligands will signal transmembrane serine/threonine kinase receptors, and this will then phosphorylate Smad2 and Smad3. This protein will then attach itself to Smad4 and relocate to the nucleus where the mesendoderm genes will begin to be transcribed.

Gastrulation.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Gastrulation.question: RA signaling also induce homeobox genes such as _____1 and Hoxa5
Gastrulation.fact: RA signaling also induce homeobox genes such as Hoxb1 and Hoxa5.

Gastrulation.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Gastrulation.question: Research has been conducted on the first _____ days of an embryo, but no known studies have been done after the 14 days
Gastrulation.fact: The countries that believe this have created a 14-day rule in which it is illegal to study or experiment on a human embryo after the 14-day period in vitro. Research has been conducted on the first 14 days of an embryo, but no known studies have been done after the 14 days.

Human embryonic development.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Human embryonic development.question: The _____ was Development and formation of the human embryo.
Human embryonic development.fact: Human embryonic development or human embryogenesis is the development and formation of the human embryo.

Human embryonic development.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Human embryonic development.question: At the beginning of the ninth week, the embryo is termed a fetus (spelled "foetus" in _____)
Human embryonic development.fact: At the beginning of the ninth week, the embryo is termed a fetus (spelled "foetus" in British English).

Human embryonic development.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Human embryonic development.question: Initially, the dividing cells, called blastomeres (blastos _____ for sprout), are undifferentiated and aggregated into a sphere enclosed within the zona pellucida of the ovum
Human embryonic development.fact: Initially, the dividing cells, called blastomeres (blastos Greek for sprout), are undifferentiated and aggregated into a sphere enclosed within the zona pellucida of the ovum.

Human embryonic development.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Human embryonic development.question: Next, another layer called the exocoelomic membrane or _____'s membrane will appear and surround the cytotrophoblast, as well as the primitive yolk sac
Human embryonic development.fact: Next, another layer called the exocoelomic membrane or Heuser's membrane will appear and surround the cytotrophoblast, as well as the primitive yolk sac.

Human embryonic development.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Human embryonic development.question: Human embryonic development covers the first eight weeks of development, which have _____ stages, called Carnegie stages
Human embryonic development.fact: Human embryonic development covers the first eight weeks of development, which have 23 stages, called Carnegie stages.

Human embryonic development.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Human embryonic development.question: Hematopoietic cells (present in the liver in greater numbers before birth than afterward), _____ cells, and connective tissue cells originate in the mesoderm
Human embryonic development.fact: Hematopoietic cells (present in the liver in greater numbers before birth than afterward), Kupffer cells, and connective tissue cells originate in the mesoderm.

Human embryonic development.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Human embryonic development.question: This recess differentiates to form most of the tympanic cavity of the middle ear, and all of the _____ or auditory tube
Human embryonic development.fact: This recess differentiates to form most of the tympanic cavity of the middle ear, and all of the Eustachian or auditory tube.

Hypoblast.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Hypoblast.question: The _____ was Embryonic inner cell mass tissue that forms the yolk sac and, later, chorion.
Hypoblast.fact: In amniote embryology, the hypoblast is one of two distinct layers arising from the inner cell mass in the mammalian blastocyst, or from the blastodisc in reptiles and birds. The hypoblast gives rise to the yolk sac.

Hypoblast.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Hypoblast.question: In between the area opaca and _____'s sickle is a belt-like region called the posterior marginal zone (PMZ)
Hypoblast.fact: In between the area opaca and Koller's sickle is a belt-like region called the posterior marginal zone (PMZ). The sheet of cells that grows anteriorly from Koller's sickle combines with the primary hypoblast to form the secondary hypoblast (also called the endoblast).

Hypoblast.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Hypoblast.question: The PMZ organizes the _____'s center in amniotes
Hypoblast.fact: The PMZ organizes the Hensen's center in amniotes.

Hypoblast.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Hypoblast.question: Some of the cells from the anterior portion of the epiblast contribute to the formation of _____'s node
Hypoblast.fact: Some of the cells from the anterior portion of the epiblast contribute to the formation of Hensen's node. The Hensen's node is the organizer for gastrulation in the vertebrate embryo.

Hypoblast.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Hypoblast.question: The first cells to migrate through _____'s node are destined to become the foregut's pharyngeal endoderm
Hypoblast.fact: The first cells to migrate through Hensen's node are destined to become the foregut's pharyngeal endoderm.

Hypoblast.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Hypoblast.question: Once formed, however, the streak secretes its _____ antagonist—the Lefty protein—which prevents further primitive streaks from forming
Hypoblast.fact: Nodal activity is needed to initiate the primitive streak, and that it is the secretion of Cerberus—an antagonist of Nodal—by the primary hypoblast cells that prevent primitive streak formation. As the primary hypoblast cells move away from the PMZ, Cerberus protein is no longer present, allowing Nodal activity (and, therefore, forming the primitive streak) in the posterior epiblast.

Hypoblast.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Hypoblast.question: As the primitive streak reaches its maximum length, transcription of the _____ hedgehog gene (Shh) becomes restricted to the embryo's left side, controlled by activin and its receptor
Hypoblast.fact: As the primitive streak reaches its maximum length, transcription of the Sonic hedgehog gene (Shh) becomes restricted to the embryo's left side, controlled by activin and its receptor.

Inner cell mass.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Inner cell mass.question: The _____ was Early embryonic mass that gives rise to the fetus.
Inner cell mass.fact: The inner cell mass (ICM) or embryoblast (known as the pluriblast in marsupials) is a structure in the early development of a mammalian embryo. The inner cell mass forms in the earliest stages of embryonic development, before implantation into the endometrium of the uterus.

Inner cell mass.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Inner cell mass.question: In contrast with Oct4, studies of _____-null mice do not show the reversion of the ICM to a TE-like morphology, but demonstrate that loss of Nanog prevents the ICM from generating primitive endoderm
Inner cell mass.fact: Nanog: Nanog is also expressed in the ICM and participates in maintaining its pluripotency. In contrast with Oct4, studies of Nanog-null mice do not show the reversion of the ICM to a TE-like morphology, but demonstrate that loss of Nanog prevents the ICM from generating primitive endoderm.

Inner cell mass.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Inner cell mass.question: Tead4: _____2, Tead4 is required for TE function, although the transcription factor is expressed ubiquitously
Inner cell mass.fact: Tead4: Like Cdx2, Tead4 is required for TE function, although the transcription factor is expressed ubiquitously. Like Cdx2-null embryos, the Tead4-null embryos can yield embryonic stem cells, indicating that Tead4 is dispensable for ICM specification.

Inner cell mass.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Inner cell mass.question: Recent work has shown that _____4 may help to upregulate Cdx2 in the TE and its transcriptional activity depends on the coactivator Yap
Inner cell mass.fact: Tead4: Like Cdx2, Tead4 is required for TE function, although the transcription factor is expressed ubiquitously. Tead4-null mice similarly undergo compaction, but fail to generate the blastocoel cavity.

Inner cell mass.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Inner cell mass.question: An apical-basolateral polarity is visible through the visualization of apical markers such as Par3, Par6, and aPKC as well as the basal marker E-_____
Inner cell mass.fact: An apical-basolateral polarity is visible through the visualization of apical markers such as Par3, Par6, and aPKC as well as the basal marker E-Cadherin.

Inner cell mass.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Inner cell mass.question: In concert with a third transcription factor, _____, these genes act to suppress pluripotency genes like Oct4 and Nanog in the outside cells
Inner cell mass.fact: In concert with a third transcription factor, Eomes, these genes act to suppress pluripotency genes like Oct4 and Nanog in the outside cells.

Inner cell mass.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Inner cell mass.question: Inside cells, however, do not turn on the Cdx2 gene, and express high levels of Oct4, _____, and Sox2
Inner cell mass.fact: In concert with a third transcription factor, Eomes, these genes act to suppress pluripotency genes like Oct4 and Nanog in the outside cells. Inside cells, however, do not turn on the Cdx2 gene, and express high levels of Oct4, Nanog, and Sox2.

Inner cell mass.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Inner cell mass.question: Blastomeres are dissociated from an isolated ICM in an early blastocyst, and their transcriptional code governed by Oct4, Sox2, and _____ helps maintain an undifferentiated state
Inner cell mass.fact: Blastomeres are dissociated from an isolated ICM in an early blastocyst, and their transcriptional code governed by Oct4, Sox2, and Nanog helps maintain an undifferentiated state.

Lateral plate mesoderm.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Lateral plate mesoderm.question: The _____ was Anatomical structure.
Lateral plate mesoderm.fact: The lateral plate mesoderm is the mesoderm that is found at the periphery of the embryo. The lateral plate mesoderm is separated from the paraxial mesoderm by a narrow region of intermediate mesoderm.

Mesoderm.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Mesoderm.question: The _____ was Middle germ layer of embryonic development.
Mesoderm.fact: The mesoderm is the middle layer of the three germ layers that develops during gastrulation in the very early development of the embryo of most animals. The mesoderm forms mesenchyme, mesothelium and coelomocytes.

Mesoderm.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Mesoderm.question: Many studies with _____ and zebrafish have analyzed the factors of this development and how they interact in signaling and transcription
Mesoderm.fact: Many studies with Xenopus and zebrafish have analyzed the factors of this development and how they interact in signaling and transcription.

Mesoderm.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Mesoderm.question: Eventually, the development of the notochord canal and the axial canal takes place between days _____ and 19, when the first three somites are formed
Mesoderm.fact: The notochord process occurs between days 15 and 17. Eventually, the development of the notochord canal and the axial canal takes place between days 17 and 19, when the first three somites are formed.

Anterior cranial fossa.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Anterior cranial fossa.question: The _____ was Part of the human skull.
Anterior cranial fossa.fact: The anterior cranial fossa is a depression in the floor of the cranial base which houses the projecting frontal lobes of the brain.

Arachnoid mater.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Arachnoid mater.question: The _____ was Web-like middle layer of the three meninges.
Arachnoid mater.fact: The arachnoid mater (or simply arachnoid) is one of the three meninges, the protective membranes that cover the brain and spinal cord. The arachnoid mater is a derivative of the neural crest mesoectoderm in the embryo.

Arachnoid mater.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Arachnoid mater.question: The arachnoid and pia mater are sometimes considered as a single structure, the leptomeninx, or the plural version, leptomeninges (lepto, from the _____ root meaning "thin" or "slender")
Arachnoid mater.fact: The arachnoid and pia mater are sometimes considered as a single structure, the leptomeninx, or the plural version, leptomeninges (lepto, from the Greek root meaning "thin" or "slender").

Arachnoid mater.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Arachnoid mater.question: The introduction of the name "arachnoid mater" is attributed to Frederik Ruysch in _____
Arachnoid mater.fact: The introduction of the name "arachnoid mater" is attributed to Frederik Ruysch in 1699.

Arachnoid mater.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Arachnoid mater.question: Another source states that the "arachnoid membrane" was discovered and named by Gerardus Blaes (Blasius) in _____, and that Ruysch adopted the term in 1692
Arachnoid mater.fact: Another source states that the "arachnoid membrane" was discovered and named by Gerardus Blaes (Blasius) in 1664, and that Ruysch adopted the term in 1692.

Arachnoid mater.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Arachnoid mater.question: Another source states that the "arachnoid membrane" was discovered and named by _____ (Blasius) in 1664, and that Ruysch adopted the term in 1692
Arachnoid mater.fact: Another source states that the "arachnoid membrane" was discovered and named by Gerardus Blaes (Blasius) in 1664, and that Ruysch adopted the term in 1692.

Base of skull.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Base of skull.question: The _____ was Inferior area of the skull.
Base of skull.fact: The base of skull, also called the cranial base or the cranial floor, is the most inferior area of the skull.

Base of skull.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Base of skull.question: Allometric growth is observed in the first trimester, with the longitudinal dimension increasing from _____ to 17 millimeters between the 8th and 14th weeks of fetal life
Base of skull.fact: Allometric growth is observed in the first trimester, with the longitudinal dimension increasing from 5 to 17 millimeters between the 8th and 14th weeks of fetal life.

Bregma.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Bregma.question: The _____ was Meeting point of the coronal suture and the sagittal suture of the skull.
Bregma.fact: The bregma is the anatomical point on the skull at which the coronal suture is intersected perpendicularly by the sagittal suture.

Bregma.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Bregma.question: The anterior fontanelle is membranous and closes in the first _____-36 months of life
Bregma.fact: The anterior fontanelle is membranous and closes in the first 18-36 months of life.

Calvaria (skull).subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Calvaria (skull).question: The _____ was Top part of the skull.
Calvaria (skull).fact: The calvaria is the top part of the skull. It is the superior part of the neurocranium and covers the cranial cavity containing the brain.

Calvaria (skull).subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Calvaria (skull).question: In _____, the word calvaria is used as a feminine noun with plural calvariae; however, many medical texts incorrectly list the word as calvarium, a neuter Latin noun with plural calvaria
Calvaria (skull).fact: In Latin, the word calvaria is used as a feminine noun with plural calvariae; however, many medical texts incorrectly list the word as calvarium, a neuter Latin noun with plural calvaria.

Calvaria (skull).subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Calvaria (skull).question: In the calvarial innervation in the adult mouse, _____-labeled fibers and peripherin were seen in the sutures, emissary canals, and bone marrow but not in diploe
Calvaria (skull).fact: In the calvarial innervation in the adult mouse, CGRP-labeled fibers and peripherin were seen in the sutures, emissary canals, and bone marrow but not in diploe.

Dacryon.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Dacryon.question: The _____ was Bone junction in the skull.
Dacryon.fact: The point of junction of the maxillary bone, lacrimal bone, and frontal bone is named the dacryon.

Diploë.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Diploë.question: The _____ was Bone in the skull.
Diploë.fact: Diploë ( or DIP-lo-ee) is the spongy cancellous bone separating the inner and outer layers of the cortical bone of the skull. The intervening cancellous tissue is called the diploë.

Dura mater.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Dura mater.question: The _____ was Outermost layer of the protective tissues around the central nervous system (meninges).
Dura mater.fact: The dura mater (or just dura) is the outermost of the three meningeal membranes. The dura mater has two layers, an outer periosteal layer closely adhered to the neurocranium, and an inner meningeal layer called the dural border cell layer.

Dura mater.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Dura mater.question: At major boundaries of brain regions such as the longitudinal fissure between the hemispheres, and the tentorium cerebelli between the posterior brain and the cerebellum the dura separates, folds and _____nates to make the divisions
Dura mater.fact: At major boundaries of brain regions such as the longitudinal fissure between the hemispheres, and the tentorium cerebelli between the posterior brain and the cerebellum the dura separates, folds and invaginates to make the divisions.

Dura mater.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Dura mater.question: In _____, researchers discovered a connective tissue bridge from the rectus capitis posterior major to the cervical dura mater
Dura mater.fact: In 2011, researchers discovered a connective tissue bridge from the rectus capitis posterior major to the cervical dura mater.

Dura mater.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Dura mater.question: Cerebellar tonsillar ectopia, or _____ malformation, is a condition that was previously thought to be congenital but can be induced by trauma, particularly whiplash trauma
Dura mater.fact: Cerebellar tonsillar ectopia, or Chiari malformation, is a condition that was previously thought to be congenital but can be induced by trauma, particularly whiplash trauma. These conditions are sometimes found in conjunction with Arnold–Chiari malformation.

Dura mater.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Dura mater.question: Dural ectasia is the enlargement of the dura and is common in connective tissue disorders, such as _____ syndrome and Ehlers–Danlos syndrome
Dura mater.fact: Dural ectasia is the enlargement of the dura and is common in connective tissue disorders, such as Marfan syndrome and Ehlers–Danlos syndrome.

Dura mater.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Dura mater.question: These conditions are sometimes found in conjunction with _____–Chiari malformation
Dura mater.fact: These conditions are sometimes found in conjunction with Arnold–Chiari malformation.

Fontanelle.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Fontanelle.question: The _____ was Anatomical feature of the infant human skull.
Fontanelle.fact: A fontanelle (or fontanel) (colloquially, soft spot) is an anatomical feature of the infant human skull comprising soft membranous gaps (sutures) between the cranial bones that make up the calvaria of a fetus or an infant. Fontanelles allow for stretching and deformation of the neurocranium both during birth and later as the brain expands faster than the surrounding bone can grow.

Fontanelle.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Fontanelle.question: It is very common in _____ syndrome and some congenital infections
Fontanelle.fact: It is very common in Down syndrome and some congenital infections.

Fontanelle.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Fontanelle.question: The American Kennel Club breed standard states that the skull of the _____ should be domed, with or without the molera being present

Fontanelle.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Fontanelle.question: In one study, the frequency of third fontanelles in an unselected population of newborn infants was _____
Fontanelle.fact: In one study, the frequency of third fontanelles in an unselected population of newborn infants was 6.3%.

Meninges.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Meninges.question: The _____ was Three membranes protecting the brain.
Meninges.fact: In anatomy, the meninges (; sing. In mammals, three meninges have been clearly identified: the dura mater, the arachnoid mater, and the pia mater.

Meninges.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Meninges.question: meninx ; from _____ μῆνινξ (mêninx) 'membrane') are protective membranes that cover the brain and spinal cord
Meninges.fact: meninx ; from Ancient Greek μῆνινξ (mêninx) 'membrane') are protective membranes that cover the brain and spinal cord.

Meninges.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Meninges.question: These layers separate to surround the _____ venous sinuses
Meninges.fact: These layers separate to surround the Dural venous sinuses. The dura mater surrounds the arachnoid mater and supports the dural sinuses which carry blood from the brain to the heart.

Meninges.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Meninges.question: The dura mater folds inwards upon itself to form four areas of infolding called dural reflections: _____ cerebri: This sickle-shaped fold is the largest of the dural reflections
Meninges.fact: The dura mater folds inwards upon itself to form four areas of infolding called dural reflections: Falx cerebri: This sickle-shaped fold is the largest of the dural reflections.

Meninges.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Meninges.question: Hippocrates described the dura in his monograph "_____ of the Head" and insisted that care should be taken to keep it intact and clean
Meninges.fact: Hippocrates described the dura in his monograph "On Injuries of the Head" and insisted that care should be taken to keep it intact and clean.

Meninges.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Meninges.question: The arachnoid layer was first described by Dutch physician Gerardus Blasius in _____
Meninges.fact: The arachnoid layer was first described by Dutch physician Gerardus Blasius in 1664.

Meninges.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Meninges.question: The arachnoid layer was first described by Dutch physician _____ in 1664

Meninges.question: In _____, Humphrey Ridley first described the subarachnoid cisterns
Meninges.fact: In 1695, Humphrey Ridley first described the subarachnoid cisterns.

Meninges.question: In 1695, _____ first described the subarachnoid cisterns
Meninges.fact: In 1695, Humphrey Ridley first described the subarachnoid cisterns.

Meninges.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy

Meninges.fact: In 1699, Frederick Ruysch confirmed that the arachnoid mater formed a complete layer that surrounded the brain.

Meninges.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Meninges.question: Arachnoid granulations were first described by Italian physician Antonio Pacchioni who published his Dissertatio Epistolaris de Glandulis Conglobatis Durae Meningis Humanae in _____
Meninges.fact: Arachnoid granulations were first described by Italian physician Antonio Pacchioni who published his Dissertatio Epistolaris de Glandulis Conglobatis Durae Meningis Humanae in 1705.

Meninges.fact: Arachnoid granulations were first described by Italian physician Antonio Pacchioni who published his Dissertatio Epistolaris de Glandulis Conglobatis Durae Meningis Humanae in 1705.

Meninges.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Meninges.question: In seven articles from _____ to 1902, Italian anatomist Giuseppe Sterzi described comparative studies on the meninges from the lancelet to the human
Meninges.fact: In seven articles from 1899 to 1902, Italian anatomist Giuseppe Sterzi described comparative studies on the meninges from the lancelet to the human.

Meninges.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Meninges.question: SDHs occur in about _____ cases of severe head trauma
Meninges.fact: SDHs occur in about 30% cases of severe head trauma.

Middle cranial fossa.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Middle cranial fossa.question: The _____ was Compound structure in the skull.
Middle cranial fossa.fact: The middle cranial fossa is formed by the sphenoid bones, and the temporal bones.

Ventral body cavity.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Ventral body cavity.question: The _____ was Cavity of the human anterior.
Ventral body cavity.fact: The ventral body cavity is a body cavity in the anterior aspect of the human body, comprising the thoracic cavity and abdominopelvic cavity.

Dugesia.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Dugesia.question: The _____ was Genus of flatworms.
Dugesia.fact: Dugesia is a genus of freshwater planarians in the family Dugesiidae triclads and the type genus of this family. Dugesia is best known to non-specialists because of its regeneration capacities.

Dugesia.subject: Animal Husbandry & Dairy
Dugesia.question: These common flatworms are found in freshwater habitats of Africa, _____, and Australia
Dugesia.fact: These common flatworms are found in freshwater habitats of Africa, Eurasia, and Australia.

Antibody-dependent cellular cytotoxicity.question: The _____ was Cell-mediated killing of other cells mediated by antibodies.
Antibody-dependent cellular cytotoxicity.fact: Antibody-dependent cellular cytotoxicity (ADCC), also called antibody-dependent cell-mediated cytotoxicity, is a mechanism of cell-mediated immune defense whereby an effector cell of the immune system kills a target cell, whose membrane-surface antigens have been bound by specific antibodies.
